nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

**Key inputs**

- **prompt**: describe the shots, camera moves, and the accompanying audio (dialogue, SFX, music) in one block
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector. H3's native canvas is a 768px short edge, capped at 768x1344 pixels, rounded to a multiple of 32
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node, snapping up to the model's 17-frame-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps

Title: Continuous music-synchronized visual metamorphosis
seamless smooth transformation, continuous dynamic camera tracking, fluid morphing motion, cinematic transition

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic music video presented as ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS SHOT from beginning to end, with no cuts and no separate shots. The image is in constant motion and continuously transforms from one visual state into another. There is never an instant replacement of the image and never a moment where one complete composition disappears and another complete composition simply appears. Instead, the visible pixels, shapes, colors, textures, objects, faces, environments, and camera perspective are constantly moving and transforming into the elements that will form the following visual state. Every transformation must contain visible intermediate states between the starting visual and the ending visual. The viewer must be able to watch the actual physical transformation happening on screen at all times. The camera continuously moves through this evolving imagery with fluid zooms, pans, rotations, pushes, pulls, and forward movement, helping connect radically different visual compositions without interruption. The visual content changes continuously and unpredictably throughout the entire duration, but the underlying motion never stops. The music controls the rate and intensity of the transformation: individual beats cause visible deformations, rhythmic accents cause shapes to stretch, ripple, rotate, split, merge, or reorganize, and stronger musical hits cause large-scale metamorphoses. Between beats, the transformation continues rather than freezing. Faster musical passages produce rapid continuous morphing, while slower passages produce longer and smoother metamorphoses. Each visual state should remain recognizable only briefly before physically flowing into another completely different visual state.

overall_soundscape: The music dominates the soundtrack. Subtle synchronized whooshes, impacts, tonal sweeps, granular textures, and transformation sounds reinforce major visual deformations without overpowering the music.

non_diegetic_music: A highly rhythmic electronic music track with a strong kick, bass, percussion, melodic accents, and clearly defined rhythmic changes. The visual transformation continuously follows the musical rhythm, with every major beat producing a visible deformation or metamorphic event and stronger musical accents producing larger continuous transformations.
